rationale: inputs/search.json allows only execution_plan this round, and the prior trial's failure evidence points at exactly that level. trial-paired-repair-a selected a joint 40-group conv->BatchNorm epilogue boundary at all 20 sites; it passed quality (max_abs_error 6.9e-6 over 1001 logits, exact top-1) but was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise (paired gains +0.1419/-0.0716 ms against MAD-derived bounds 0.0331/0.0431 ms; candidate wall became bimodal, 1.1872 vs 1.4145 ms). The framework's per-group before/after CUDA evidence shows why the edit could not clear the bound: the fold removed the 43.84 us of aten.batch_norm kernel time, but the 20 convolutions re-ran with a bias epilogue under slower cudnn heuristic choices - 4dbe179ff990714f37f0d969 regressed 39.648->55.818 us and 6214ff32dc254755c8d920f5 was flat at 118.846->119.094 us - so inclusive CUDA time across the 20 replaced sites actually rose ~2.9 us (13.5 us of per-site savings vs 16.4 us of regressions), while the candidate added 20 per-repeat Python guard dispatches and +46.5 MB of resident folded weights (peak allocated 86,361,088 -> 132,884,480 B). A kernel-time-neutral, dispatch-adding edit cannot beat a 33-43 us noise bound, and that is a property of the regime, not of the fold's algebra. The measured structure of this frozen workload shows the regime: the complete-workload call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 covers 731.385 us of GPU work in 81 CUDA kernels (coverage: 81/81 associated), but reference wall latency_ms is 1.336024 - a ~605 us (45.3%) per-forward gap charged by the eager delivery mechanism: 188 op dispatches per repeat (119 nn.Module __call__ inversions plus 69 aten op invocations), dozens of 1-4 us kernels in stages 0-2 (e.g. 1.1-2.8 us ReLUs, 1.7-2.5 us residual add_s, 8-12 us convs) that CPU dispatch cannot feed at ~3.2 us of non-kernel wall time per dispatched op. The previous trial demonstrated both halves of the trap: local kernel-time edits of that scale (~44 us) vanish inside this gap plus noise, and a faster local kernel need not move latency_ms at all. The coherent editable boundary is therefore the whole timed forward, selected at the two nested spans the framework targets and which enclose the identical 731.385 us region: the complete-workload group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) and the ResNetForImageClassification group 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef (model forward, 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2, pixel_values [1,3,224,224] fp32 cuda). affected_calls is the entire subtree of that invoke: every observed module call, every aten call, and the instrumentation calls interleaved among them - 269 calls in all - because re-planning execution at this level changes the delivery of every one of them and none of them should be individually re-edited. The opportunity is to change how the frozen kernel DAG is delivered per repeat, not which kernels run: capture the unchanged eager forward once at build time (warmup and capture on a side stream into static input/output buffers), then per timed repeat copy the adapter's pixels into the static input, replay the captured graph, and return the static logits (cloned). The exact kernel sequence, FP32/TF32-off, cudnn-benchmark-off policies and the real fixture values are preserved, so no call is reordered, no alias or persistent state is introduced, and unknown cross-stream dependencies are respected by keeping the captured stream DAG identical to the eager one; any input not matching the captured shape/stride/dtype/device signature falls back to the unmodified eager forward. Per-op kernel work stays out of this round on purpose: the stage-3 conv inefficiency is real (bcb576ff7b303e075fb61f51, 256->512 stride-2 3x3, 115.966 us at ~1.0 TFLOP/s vs 30.848/36.544 us for its same-FLOP 115.6 MF stride-2 siblings 85e362c8893edef501c6b5c8/52801fdcf001973dc9b22a3b, plus c2db48d097463651f51bd75c, the three 512x512x3x3 @7x7 convs, 204.125 us at ~3.4 TFLOP/s vs ~19.0 us each for same-FLOP convs at 28x28; together 43.8% of region GPU time), but it belongs to per-op scopes that are not allowed here, and the rejected trial is direct evidence that such local gains do not by themselves move the project metric.
hypothesis: Replacing the per-repeat eager dispatch of the frozen batch=1 FP32 forward with a build-time-captured whole-forward execution (one capture of the unchanged model(pixel_values=...).logits sequence on a side stream; per timed repeat: copy the fixed pixels into the static input, graph replay, clone/observe the static logits) removes most of the ~605 us per-forward non-kernel wall cost of 188 eager op dispatches and 81 kernel launches while executing the identical kernel DAG on identical input values, so logits and top-1 are expected to reproduce the reference exactly (same kernels, same order, deterministic cudnn heuristics with benchmark off) and paired median latency_ms is expected to fall from ~1.336 ms to ~0.75-0.90 ms, i.e. paired gains of roughly 0.4-0.55 ms in both AB and BA pairings - an order of magnitude above the 0.033-0.043 ms noise bounds that rejected the previous candidate. This is a hypothesis to be tested, not assumed: capture must prove capture-safe for this forward (conv/batch_norm/relu/pool/add_/linear/flatten only, no host syncs or .item() in the timed path); the static-input copy and output clone (~10-30 us) are real costs that must stay small; the graph's private memory pool must not materially regress peak_allocated_bytes from the 86,361,088 B baseline (the previous candidate's +46.5 MB shows the memory check bites); and worker-side one-time capture must stay outside the timed region in fresh AB/BA workers. Acceptance requires both paired gains above their MAD-derived noise bounds with logits within atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top-1, and math_policy_unchanged; any capture failure, tolerance failure, memory regression, or gain not above noise triggers atomic fallback to the unmodified eager execution.
